title: Capacity-cell political context varies sharply by party identity as well as place
source_unit: 2024 Cooperative Election Study common-content post-election respondent with county FIPS and pid7, assigned to 2023 county CBP health-establishment and ACS zero-vehicle context cell
geography: United States; 620 counties with at least 100,000 residents and valid 2020/2023 population estimates

observations.period: 2024; CES capacity/mobility context; high health capacity / high zero-vehicle share; Democratic-leaning (pid7 1–3)

denominator.unit: CES respondents; 188 capacity-frame counties; population frame counties >=100,000

median_population_change_pct.unit: percent county population change, 2020–2023; median within capacity cell

federal_trust.unit: percent trusting federal government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

state_trust.unit: percent trusting state government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

civic_action.unit: percent reporting at least one selected civic action; commonpostweight

reported_voted.unit: percent reporting definitely voted in November 2024; commonpostweight

observations.method: Weighted descriptive CES comparison within broad pid7 party groups after county-keyed assignment to CBP health-establishment/ACS zero-vehicle cells; party groups code pid7 1–3 as Democratic-leaning, 4 as Independent, and 5–7 as Republican-leaning; health cut 28.312 and zero-vehicle cut 5.606.
observations.uncertainty: No complex-survey standard errors or county-representative estimates; party identity is a descriptive conditioning variable, not a pre-exposure causal control here, and smaller other/unknown cells are especially unstable.
observations.subgroup: CES respondents in Democratic-leaning (pid7 1–3) and the high health capacity / high zero-vehicle share capacity/mobility context cell.
observations.counterinterpretation: Party identity, selection, county composition, local growth, and question universe can structure trust and action; subgroup differences do not show that capacity or mobility caused political response.

related_sources.claim: CES 2024 common-content public data supply county FIPS, pid7, trust, civic-action, vote, and commonpostweight fields.
2023 CBP health/social-assistance establishment counts used for capacity cell assignment.
2023 ACS zero-vehicle-household counts used for mobility cell assignment.
Reproduction script for party-conditioned county capacity cells and weighted endpoints.

boundary: This is a same-county contextual subgroup comparison, not a same-respondent causal exposure. It does not establish that local business/service capacity or vehicle constraints caused trust, civic action, or voting; party groups are descriptive, and CES/county administrative/ACS layers retain separate denominators and uncertainty.
